extracted.intended_audience: comics scholars, digital humanities researchers, and computer-vision/data-science researchers studying comic strips
extracted.subtask_description: Computational/distant viewing analysis of newspaper comic strips (Panles, captions, paratext) using panel-detection and OCR-based caption detection to study formal features across a large corpus (Peanuts, 1950–2000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel visual definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Every panel we found was enclosed in a black, rectangular, apparently hand-drawn box. These boxes are arranged in a non-overlapping fashion on a white background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional observation motivates treating contiguous non-background pixel regions bounded by white background as candidate panels; it is the basis for a rules-based panel detection algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel detection algorithm (flood-fill/tint-fill approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: First, determine all of the pixels reachable by starting at a white pixel on an edge and creating a path of adjacent white pixels (the background). Next, select any non-background pixel and determine the set of all non-background pixels reachable via adjacent non-background pixels (a detected panel). Repeat until all pixels are accounted for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation used a breadth-first adaptation of the tint fill algorithm (Smith 1976) in custom C code. After detection, remove very small panels (usually extraneous writing), expand detected panels to full rectangles, and number panels according to reading order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove tiny/extraneous panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Very small detected panels are usually extraneous writing on the background and should be removed from panel counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter out small connected components prior to expanding detections to full rectangular panel bounding boxes to avoid counting stray marks or paratext as panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand detected panels to full rectangles
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying contiguous non-background pixel regions, expand the detected panels to be full rectangles for downstream processing and numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rectangular expansion simplifies later operations (e.g., mapping OCR bounding boxes into panel coordinate space) and aligns with newspaper strip panel geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel numbering convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Number panels according to the standard left-to-right and top-to-bottom reading order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this canonical ordering when aggregating per-panel statistics across strips (e.g., caption presence in panel 1 vs panel 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel detection validation (manual inspection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate algorithmic panel detection by manually inspecting a random sample of comics (authors report manual inspection of 135 randomly selected comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors found only a single error in 135 comics, demonstrating high accuracy; include sample size and error counts when reporting detection reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption detection algorithm selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply scene text detection algorithms (Baek et al. 2019) as implemented in the EasyOCR Python module to provide bounding boxes for all detected text in an image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a modern scene-text/OCR method suitable for hand-lettered/stylized comic lettering; document implementation and library versions (e.g., EasyOCR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude signatures and paratext from caption counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Schulz commonly signed each Peanuts comic at the bottom of the last panel; to remove the signature from counts, automatically remove all text in the bottom third of the last panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtering by spatial heuristics (bottom third of last panel) helps exclude signatures, dates, and copyright lines; note that signatures are detected about half the time and should not be considered captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption detection validation (manual sample and error reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually validate caption detection on a random sample (authors used 100 comics). Report false detections and sources of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors report low false-detection rates (very few false positives/negatives); most errors derive from stylized exclamations and sound effects. Always report validation sample size and error counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine panel and caption detections to localize captions within panels
rubrics_metrics.description: After detecting panel rectangles and text bounding boxes, indicate which panels in each cartoon have text located within them to determine caption presence and position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combination permits per-panel caption presence statistics and analyses of the image-text relationship (e.g., caption position tendencies across panel indices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat dailies and Sundays separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily strips and Sunday strips differ in format (daily: typically 1x3 or 1x4 horizontal grid, black-and-white; Sunday: larger, color, more panels). Average panel lengths differ and should be analyzed separately (authors report daily avg ~3.74, Sunday avg ~9.49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate analyses by publication format (daily vs Sunday) because layout constraints and narrative possibilities differ substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus composition and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a large, well-defined corpus (the study uses the complete Peanuts run: 17,897 cartoons, 1950–2000) and document limits (e.g., 2000 incomplete due to Schulz's death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly report corpus size, date range, and any completeness caveats or missing data when presenting large-scale findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative reporting of panel/caption statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: After detection, compute and report statistics such as average panel counts by day/year and per-panel caption-presence percentages (e.g., in four-panel strips: first panel contains text 98% of the time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present year-by-year visualizations and aggregated percentages to reveal longitudinal trends (e.g., shift away from four-panel format beginning 1988).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address algorithmic misdetections via manual follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: When visualizations/outputs show anomalies (e.g., extra detected panels in certain strips or years), perform manual inspection to determine if misdetections occurred and report corrections or their causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: five strips in 1975 where algorithm detected panels that did not exist; manual checks confirmed four-panel layout. Document such audits and how they informed adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document sources of OCR/vision error
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and report common error sources: stylized lettering, sound effects, hard-to-detect lettering, and paratext elements that can be mistaken for dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report these limitations and, when possible, quantify their impact on detection accuracy; consider targeted heuristics or pre-/post-processing to mitigate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and code/supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Include full code implementing custom algorithms in supplementary materials to enable reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide implementation details (language, libraries, custom C code for tint fill, EasyOCR versions) and sample sizes used for validation so others can reproduce and extend the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution integrating formal results with historical/contextual factors
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreting changes in format (e.g., Schulz's move away from four-panel dailies in 1988), consider editorial constraints, syndicate policies, artist agency, health (e.g., essential tremor), and industry practices rather than ascribing single causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize computational findings with archival/interview evidence (e.g., curator or interview statements) and acknowledge alternative explanations.
